title: Curve modeling
summary: Patch 0024 brings curve modelling to the mesh editor: a Curve modeling tab where curves are sketched on any surface and turned into solids - extruded, revolved, lofted, swept, piped or filled - that stay tied to their curves, every step editable any time, with curve booleans, an overview of solids and parts, and edge fillets. A solid can be baked into one clean mesh whose curves are its edges: drag any edge point and the faces follow, and when you let go it settles into a tidy grid of quads, rebuilt where it stretched. Points move smoothly along the axis your drag suggests, with guides that line them up; double-click to insert or dissolve points, right-click to make one smooth or sharp. A wireframe view, a preview of the model in the running game, and a right-click menu that folds open with a glint round its edge complete it.

steps.title: A Curve modeling tab
steps.text: The mesh editor's right panel and its right-click menu now have two tabs: Mesh, with everything they had, and Curve modeling. Curves are sketched on a construction plane - the surface under your first click, the ground, the front, the side, the view or the selection's plane - with six tools (line, spline, circle, arc, rectangle, polygon), snapping to the grid and to other curves' points, typed sizes, and the curves are saved beside the model.

diagram.text: sketch on any surface, the ground or the view

steps.title: Solids that follow their curves
steps.text: Extrude, revolve, loft, sweep, pipe and fill make solids that stay tied to their curves: move a point and the solid is made again at once. Each solid is a recipe of steps - every height, angle and radius editable any time in the SOLID box's recipe tree - and any curve can cut, join or intersect, each with its own height. Solids can be positive or negative, and the solids cut away show as ghosts.

the recipe tree:
edit any step

diagram.text: move a point: the solid is made again at once

steps.title: Curve booleans and lean curves
steps.text: Curves can be united, subtracted and intersected - on one plane or across planes - leaving lean results: straight sides as two points, arcs as true arcs on a new path curve, smooth or sharp at each point. Simplify curve trims a dense outline down to its corners and a point every 40 degrees along its bends. Curves move, turn and scale in 3D like the mesh, X / Y / Z for an axis.

diagram.text: results as lean as the shapes they describe

steps.title: Overview and parts
steps.text: The OVERVIEW tree lists every solid with its curves and each recipe step under it: click to select, hide with the eye, rename with F2 or the right-click menu, which also offers each row's own actions. Solids are grouped into parts - a part moves, turns and scales as one - and the Mesh tab gets an overview of its own.

diagram.text: every row with its own tooltip

steps.title: Bake a solid: its curves are its edges
steps.text: Bake turns a solid - with every solid touching it - into one baked solid whose curves are the edges of its mesh: corner to corner, as few points as keep their shape. Its walls and flat faces are rows and columns of quads, the mesh closed. Move an edge's point in any direction and the faces at it follow, solved smooth; when you let go the solid settles - columns made straight, stretched four-sided faces rebuilt as a grid for their new shape, sharp bends given loop cuts - and that is its new start. Shading is smooth across curves and sharp at every real edge.

diagram.text: BAKE: THE CURVES ARE ITS EDGES

diagram.label:
one solid, the
touching ones in

steps.title: Editing points: smart, smooth, guided
steps.text: Dragging a point or a curve no longer jumps: it moves from where you pressed, along the X, Y or Z axis that runs closest to your drag on screen (drawn through it in its colour, with the distance), smoothly - Ctrl for grid steps. Guides snap it level with other points (its own curve's first) or with a flat face, a dashed line showing to what. Double-click a curve to insert a point, a point to dissolve it; right-click a point for Smooth or Sharp. Curves behind a solid are hidden.

diagram.text: nothing jumps: every drag starts from where you pressed

steps.title: Wireframe and preview in game
steps.text: The toolbar's Wireframe (Shift+W) draws every part's edges over it - quads as quads, hidden lines hidden - to spot a stretched or folded patch at a glance. Preview in game sets the model down in front of you in the running game to walk or fly round it, F8 or Esc to come back - from the title too, Talos carried into your latest save with its undo history. Both are icon-only buttons.

diagram.text: see the mesh as it is, and the model where it'll be

steps.title: A menu that folds and shines
steps.text: The right-click menu unfolds from the top as it opens, its icons fading in, and folds back up as it closes - a click elsewhere or Esc too. A glint with a lens flare's cross runs round its edge once every eight seconds, a dimmer one opposite. The repository gained a README and the GPL-3.0 licence.

diagram.text: A MENU THAT FOLDS AND SHINES

review.intro: The code behind patch 0024: curve modelling in the mesh editor - scripts/editor/mesh/curve_tools.gd (the tab: sketching, editing, solids made from curves, the recipe tree, the overview, parts, baking, dragging with guides), scripts/editor/mesh/edge_net.gd (baked solids: edges traced from the mesh, walls and flat faces as quads, the smooth solve that moves them, settling, shading), mesh_bevel.gd (Fillet), model_preview.gd (Preview in game), edge_shine.gd (the menu's glint), and the hooks in the mesh editor.

@@ -1,0 +1,96 @@ # Space Atrapos
+# Space Atrapos
+
+A procedural 3D space game made with [Godot 4](https://godotengine.org/). You are an automaton in
+**New Hellas**, a galaxy of 120 star systems where six star empires of ancient Greece, the
+independents and the pirates compete. Fly your ship between stars and planets, land on worlds of
+procedural ground and walk them, trade, mine, fight, dock at stations and make your own way. There is
+no story to follow: the galaxy is yours.
+
+![Flying over Amnissos, the Minoans' ocean world](data/docs/shots/space3d.jpg)
+
+## What's in it
+
+- **A whole galaxy to fly**: 120 star systems with their own suns, planets and moons, linked by gates
+  and a hyperspace drive, with a living economy, traders, wars between the empires and reputations
+  to earn or lose.
+- **Real worlds to land on**: every planet is procedural ground on a cube sphere, streamed in as you
+  come down from orbit, with seas, coasts, clouds, caves, towns, flora and fauna.
+- **On foot and aboard**: stand up from the pilot's seat, walk out of your ship through its doors, into
+  towns, station hangars and concourses, caves and dungeons. A jet pack, a rifle, a mining beam, a
+  scanner and a builder go with you.
+- **Six empires, each with its own look**: ships, stations, towns, people and hangars for the Minoans,
+  Mycenaeans, Athenians, Spartans, Ionians and Cycladic islanders.
+- **Talos, the game's own editor**: data editors for everything in the game, a mesh editor with curve
+  modelling (sketches, procedural solids, booleans, baked solids shaped by their edges), animation
+  and effects editors, all live-editable over a running game.
+- **Mods**: mods are folders of files laid out like the game's own, mounted over it at start-up,
+  with a mod editor to make them.
+- **Built-in documentation**: a pilot's guide, a tutorial, an encyclopedia and the editor's manual,
+  in the game's Archive (F1), with annotated screenshots.
+
+![Minoan androids in a town](data/docs/shots/space3d_people.jpg)
+
+![The planet map](data/docs/shots/planet3d.jpg)
+
+## Running it
+
+1. Install [Git LFS](https://git-lfs.com/) **before cloning**: images, models, audio and fonts are
+   stored in LFS.
+
+   ```sh
+   git lfs install
+   git clone https://github.com/kilon/space-atrapos.git
+   ```
+
+2. Install **Godot 4.7** (the standard build, not .NET).
+3. Open the project in Godot and run it (F5), or from a terminal:
+
+   ```sh
+   godot --path space-atrapos
+   ```
+
+The first start imports the assets, which takes a while; later starts are quick.
+
+## Controls (the basics)
+
+| | |
+|---|---|
+| Steer the ship | the mouse (a virtual stick); **A / D** roll |
+| Throttle | **W / S** (stops at zero; again for reverse), **X** stop, **Shift** boost |
+| Thrusters | **R / F** up and down, **Q / E** sideways |
+| Land / take off | **L** (near a station: ask for a landing pad) |
+| Stand up / walk | **U** out of the seat, **W A S D**, **Space** jump (hold: jet pack) |
+| Fire / use | left mouse button |
+| The Automaton (inventory, maps, archive) | **Tab** |
+| The guide | **F1** |
+| Talos, the editor | **F8** |
+
+Everything can be rebound in **Settings > Controls**, and gamepads are supported.
+
+## For developers
+
+- **Code layout**: `scripts/core` (engine-level services), `scripts/sim` (the game's rules and data,
+  no visuals), `scripts/world` (the 3D world), `scripts/ui` (the HUD and menus), `scripts/editor`
+  (Talos). Scenes are in `scenes/`, shaders in `shaders/`.
+- **Tests**: `python3 tools/test.py` runs the whole suite in parallel, each process with its own
+  throwaway user data. Filter it with `python3 tools/test.py <file filter> [<test name filter>]`.
+- **Frame rate**: the game aims for 600 FPS and never freezes while loading.
+  `python3 tools/fps_test.py` plays it in a window and checks.
+- **Live coding**: start the game with `-- --live`, then `python3 tools/live.py` inspects it, runs
+  code in it and hot-reloads scripts while it runs.
+- **Documentation screenshots**: `python3 tools/doc_shots.py` retakes the guide's annotated shots.
+- **Characters**: the characters are generated in Blender by the scripts in `external/blender`
+  (`blender -b --python build.py -- <character> model`, then `actions` and `export`). Hand edits are
+  layered over them from `external/blender_overrides`.
+- **Patch notes**: every change is tracked between patches (`python3 tools/patch.py status`) and
+  published as an illustrated entry in the game's Patch Notes screen.
+
+## License
+
+Space Atrapos is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the
+GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, version 3 of the License.
+It is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but **without any warranty**; without even the
+implied warranty of merchantability or fitness for a particular purpose. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for
+the full text.
+
+Copyright © 2026 kilon.

@@ -272,6 +273,9 @@ ## mesh-inset | Inset | keywords: Inset
 ## mesh-inset | Inset | keywords: Inset
 **Inset** (**I**, the **EDIT MESH** row, the right-click menu) makes a ring of new faces inside the border of the selected faces - the selection inset as one region, so faces side by side share the ring round them all, and a single face gets a smaller face inside it with a quad along each of its sides. Move the mouse towards the selection's middle to widen the ring (started near the middle: the further it's moved, the wider), or type the width in metres (digits and a point; Backspace takes one back). Each corner goes in so that the ring is as wide along every side. Click or Enter keeps it, right-click or Esc cancels - nothing changes. The inner faces are selected afterwards, ready to extrude; it's one undo step. A selection with no border (a whole closed part) has nothing to inset from.
 
+## mesh-fillet | Fillet | keywords: Fillet, chamfer, bevel
+**Fillet** (**Ctrl+B**, the **EDIT MESH** row, the right-click menu) rounds off the selected edges (in face mode, the border of the selected faces; a whole closed selection - every edge between them). Each edge between two faces becomes a strip of quads whose profile is an arc touching both faces; its sides move back along the faces by the width. Move the mouse away from the selection's middle to widen it (towards: narrower), or type the width in metres (digits and a point; Backspace takes one back). The **wheel** or **+ / -** sets the segments - the rows of quads across (4 to start, then as many as last time; **1** is a flat chamfer). The width is held where it would push corners past each other (the hint says so). Where filleted edges meet, the corner is closed: one edge ending - its arc becomes part of the face across the end; two going on through a point - their arcs join in a mitre; three or more - a rounded fan. A closed part stays closed. Click or Enter keeps it, right-click or Esc cancels - nothing changes. The new strips are selected afterwards; it's one undo step.
+
 ## mesh-loop-cut | Loop cut | keywords: Loop cut
 **Loop cut** (**Ctrl+R**, the **EDIT MESH** row, the right-click menu) adds a new edge loop round a ring of quads:
 - Point at an edge: the ring across it shows - through each quad to its opposite side, on to the next quad, stopping at a triangle, an n-gon or an open border, or all the way round (a box, a cylinder, an arm).

 - The result replaces A; B is removed - or, with **Keep B (hidden)**, hidden (the eye in the parts list shows it again). Each surface keeps its material; the faces B cuts into A take B's. One **Undo** takes it all back.
 - It's worked out in the background (two parts of 2,000 triangles each take a few hundredths of a second). Both parts must be **closed** solids: a plane, or a mesh with a hole in its skin, is refused, and the note says why. A part skinned to a skeleton can't take part (its weights would be lost).
 
+## mesh-curves | Curve modeling | keywords: Curve modeling, Line, Spline, Circle, Arc, Rectangle, Polygon
+The right panel's second tab (and the right-click menu's): model hard surfaces the quick way - **draw an outline, then pull it into a solid**. Curves are drawn on a **construction plane**, snapped to its grid and to points; picked and reshaped by dragging their points; then [extruded, revolved, lofted, swept or piped](doc:mesh-curves-solids) into new parts. A model's curves are kept with it (saved beside it as `<model>.curves.json`, in its variant) and shown over the view in blue (picked: amber, their points as white squares).
+- **Wireframe** (the toolbar's Wireframe button, **Shift+W**): the parts' edges drawn over them in object mode - every quad as a quad (its two triangles' shared edge left out), edges behind a surface hidden - to see a stretched or folded patch at a glance.
+- **Sketch tools** (keys work while the Curve modeling tab is open): **Line** (**L**) - click points, a polyline; **Spline** (**P**) - a smooth curve through the points you click; **Circle** (**C**) - its centre, then the rim; **Arc** (**Shift+C**) - its start, its end, then a point it passes through; **Rectangle** (**Shift+R**) - two opposite corners (**Alt** held: from the centre); **Polygon** (**Shift+P**) - the centre, then a corner (the wheel or **+ / -**: how many sides).
+- A line or spline: **click its first point** to close it into a loop; **Enter**, **right-click** or a double click ends it open; **Backspace** takes back the last point. The tool stays on for the next curve; **Esc** stops it (with points placed: drops them first).
+- **Typed sizes**: while drawing, type a number and **Enter** - a line's next segment that long (the way the mouse points), a circle's or polygon's radius, a rectangle's "width height". The distance from the last point shows beside the cursor.
+- **Undo** (**Ctrl+Z**) takes back each curve and each change to one.
+
+## mesh-curves-overview | The overview | keywords: Overview, Part, New part from the selected, Ungroup, Move to part
+At the top of the Curve modeling tab, the **OVERVIEW** lists the whole model as a tree: first the **parts** - each a group of solids (with theirs under it) - then **Solids** in no part (each with the curves it's made from under it - a cut curve marked "(cut)"), **Meshes** (plain parts) and **Curves** no solid uses yet.
+- **Parts (groups of solids):** select some solids, right-click one: **New part from the selected** - they're grouped into a part (saved in the glb, a part of the model: the Mesh tab's list shows it too, with its solids under it). Move the part and its solids move together - their curves with them. A new solid made while a solid of a part is selected joins that part. Right-click a part: Select its solids, Hide / Show, Duplicate, **Ungroup**, Delete (with its solids); a solid: **Move to part ›** (or out of it).
+- The Mesh tab's **parts list** is the same kind of overview: parts with their solids and meshes under them; click a part to select all of it, right-click a row for its menu (Hide / Show, Duplicate, Delete, New part from the selected, Move to ›, Ungroup...), double-click to rename.
+- **Dragging a curve's point:** it moves on the curve's plane; **X / Y / Z** while dragging lock it to that axis (again: free) - lift it, lower it.
+- **Rename:** right-click a part, solid or curve - **Rename** - or select it and press **F2** (or double-click its row); type the name, Enter.
+- **Move, turn, scale a part as one:** in object mode, **G / R / S** (and the gizmo) move every selected solid together, round their middle; when all of a part's solids are selected (click the part's row), the part itself moves - its solids stay in it. One undo step.
+- **Click** a solid or a curve to select it; **Ctrl / Shift+click** for more - solids and curves together. It's the same selection the view and the boxes below use: pick two solids to join them, a solid's curves to drag or reshape them, a curve to see its CURVE box...
+- Under each solid: its own curves, and each **tool step** ("Cut: an extrusion"...) as a row of its own with that step's curves under it - click a step to select its solid and pick its curves.
+- **Right-click** a row for its menu:
+  - a **solid**: Hide / Show, Duplicate, Delete, Pick its curves, Make plain mesh, Detach its last tool, **Attach to ›** another solid (cut from / join to / common with it - live);
+  - a **tool step**: Role (Cut / Join / Common), Hide / Show its ghost, **Detach** (a solid of its own again), **Attach to ›** another solid (moved there), Delete step (its curves stay);
+  - a **curve**: Hide / Show, Pick, Duplicate, Delete, **Detach from** its solid (taken out of its step; a tool step with no other curve goes with it), **Attach to ›** a solid (a new cut / join / common step).
+- **Double-click** a name to rename it. The **eye** hides or shows it, everything it shows in the view: a solid and its ghosts; a curve, and the ghost of a tool made only of hidden curves; a tool step's ghost. (Hidden is only for seeing: the solid's shape doesn't change. One **Undo** step.)
+
+## mesh-curves-plane | The construction plane and snapping | keywords: Auto plane, Ground plane, Front plane, Side plane, View plane, Selection's plane, Snap to the grid, Grid step, Snap to points, Guides
+- The plane is picked in the **Plane** dropdown under the sketch tools. **Auto** (the default): the plane is the **surface under your first click** - click on a part's face and the curve is drawn flat on it - or, in empty space, the ground. **Ground** (X and Z), **Front** (X and Y), **Side** (Z and Y), **View** (square to the view) or **Selection** (through the selected faces in edit mode, or the picked curve) fix it. While a tool is on, the plane shows as a faint grid round the cursor.
+- **Grid** snaps points to the plane's grid (**Grid step**, 0.05 m at first); **Points** snaps them to the curves' points, ends, middles of sides and centres, and to the parts' corners - the ring at the cursor is coloured by what it caught. Hold **Ctrl** for no snapping.
+
+## mesh-curves-edit | Editing curves | keywords: Move curves, Turn curves, Scale curves, Simplify curve, Delete curves, Duplicate curves, Mirror curves, Radial array, Insert point, Dissolve point, Smooth point, Sharp point, Offset curve, Fillet corners, Join curves, Bridge curve, Reverse curve, Close / open, Union curves, Subtract curves, Intersect curves
+- **Click a curve** in the view to pick it (**Shift+click**: more, or one off again); a click in empty space lets them go. Drag a picked curve's **point** to move it, or the **curve itself** to move it whole - smoothly, from where you pressed: after a few pixels the drag picks the axis (X, Y or Z) that runs closest to your drag on screen, drawn through it in its colour (X red, Y green, Z blue) with how far it's gone; **X / Y / Z** while dragging switch to that axis (the same again: free on the axis plane facing you); **Shift** as you start (or Perspective move in the menu): free on that plane; **Ctrl**: whole grid steps. **Guides** (on by default - the Guides box by Points; **Alt** while dragging: off): when a dragged point's X, Y or Z comes within a few pixels of another point's (its own curve's first) or of a flat face's level, it snaps there and a dashed guide in that axis's colour shows to what ("Y same as a point on this curve", "Y level with a flat face"). **Double-click a curve** to put a point into it where you clicked (a circle, an arc or a bezier becomes a path of points first - the same shape). **Double-click a point** to dissolve it - the curve runs on between its neighbours (an arc's middle point: a straight line; a curve keeps at least two points, a closed one three; a baked solid's edge keeps its ends). The solids hide the curves behind them: only what you'd see of a curve is drawn, and picked. **Right-click a picked curve's point** for **Smooth point** (the curve bends smoothly through it) or **Sharp point** (a corner: straight sides either side of it) - the curve becomes a path of points, each smooth or sharp.
+- **In 3D:** with curves picked, **Move curves** (**G**) moves them over the plane facing you - up, down, anywhere; **Turn curves** (**R**) turns them about their middle (round the line of sight); **Scale curves** (**S**) scales them about their middle. **X / Y / Z** while doing it: along (or about) that axis - again: free. Moves snap to the grid and turns to 15° (**Ctrl**: free); type a number for an exact distance, angle or factor. Click or **Enter** keeps it, **Esc** or right-click cancels. A curve's plane turns with it, and the solids made from it follow. (With curves picked, G / R / S work on them rather than the part.)
+- **Delete curves** (**X / Delete**), **Duplicate curves** (**Shift+D**), **Mirror curves** (a copy across the model's X), **Radial array** (six round the Y axis).
+- **Offset curve** - a copy moved out (or in) by a distance in its plane: corners stay mitred, a circle's radius grows. The mouse sets it, or type it and **Enter**.
+- **Fillet corners** - the corners of lines, rectangles and polygons rounded (the mouse or a typed radius; 0: sharp again). The radius stays with the curve: its points still drag, the rounding follows.
+- **Union curves**, **Subtract curves**, **Intersect curves** - booleans of closed curves, worked out on the **first picked** curve's plane: pick two or more, and they're replaced by the result (one **Undo** step). Curves on other planes are brought onto it along its normal: on a parallel plane (lifted or lowered) they land as they are (a lifted circle cuts the same circle); at an angle they're projected - as seen square-on from the first one (a tilted circle cuts an ellipse); one standing edge-on to it is left out. The note says which were brought down, projected or left out. Union makes one outline (a gap they enclose becomes a hole); Subtract takes the others from the **first picked** - curves inside it become its holes; Intersect keeps what they all share. Extrude or fill the results together: a solid with its holes, still following its curves. The results are lean: a curve that comes through whole stays as it was (a circle hole is still a circle), the rest become **paths** - corners and straight sides kept as they are; a bend that's part of a circle drawn as that exact arc through its ends and one middle point; other bends get smooth points spread evenly along them. A circle minus another overlapping it is four points.
+- **Simplify curve** - the picked closed curves with more points than they need (a dense outline) made lean the same way; solids made from them follow.
+- **Join curves** - two open curves made one at their nearest ends. **Bridge curve** - a smooth curve between the nearest ends of two picked curves, leaving each along its own direction (its two handles drag). **Reverse curve** - runs the other way. **Close / open** - a line or spline made a loop, or opened.
+
+## mesh-curves-solids | Solids from curves | keywords: Extrude, Revolve, Loft, Sweep, Pipe, Fill, Steps round, Push / pull faces, Fillet edges, Inset faces
+Each makes a **new part** (one **Undo** takes it back). Closed curves make **closed solids**, facing out, so the [booleans](doc:mesh-boolean) work on them; open curves make sheets (walls). The solids are [procedural](doc:mesh-curves-procedural): they follow their curves.
+- **Holes:** closed curves inside a closed curve (in its plane) are holes - pick the outline and the curves inside it, then **Extrude** or **Fill**: a plate with its holes, no boolean needed. A curve inside a hole is a solid again (an island).
+- **Extrude** (**E** with curves picked) - pushed along their plane's normal. The mouse sets how far (a preview shows; snapped to the grid step, **Ctrl**: free), or type it; click or **Enter** makes it, **Esc** or right-click cancels. Sharp corners stay crisp, rounded ones smooth.
+- **Revolve** - the profile turned round an axis: a two-point line picked with it, else the model's Y axis (a curve drawn on the ground: its X line). The mouse sets the angle (by 15°, **Ctrl**: by 1°) or type it; 360° closes it. **Steps round** sets how smooth.
+- **Loft** - a skin through the picked curves, in the order you picked them (closed ones capped; loops wound either way are lined up).
+- **Sweep** - the first picked curve (the profile) carried along the second (the path), turned with it without twisting.
+- **Pipe** - a round tube along each picked curve (the mouse or a typed radius); a closed curve makes a ring.
+- **Fill** - closed curves filled with flat faces.
+- **On the mesh** (edit mode): **Push / pull faces** (the selected faces pulled out or in), **Fillet edges** (the selected edges rounded), **Inset faces**, **Flatten** - the mesh tools that go with curve modeling, at hand in the same tab.
+
+## mesh-curves-procedural | Procedural solids: they follow their curves | keywords: SOLID, Height, Angle, Radius, Steps, Both ways, Role, Curve role, Ghosts, Add, Picked curves, Other solid, Separate, Curve name, Corner radius, Closed, Pick its curves, Make plain mesh, Negative, Make the cut positive, Bake, Rename
+A solid made from curves keeps its **recipe** - which curves, which operation, its height / angle / radius and steps - and is **made again from its curves whenever they change**: drag a curve's point and the solid reshapes as you drag; round a curve's corners, offset it, undo or redo a change - the solid follows. Its material stays.
+- Select the solid (a part) and the Curve modeling tab shows its **SOLID** box with its whole **recipe** - every step, editable at any time, made again at once (each change one **Undo** step): an extrusion's **height** (minus: the other way) and **Both ways** (half each side of its curves' plane), a revolve's **angle** and **steps**, a pipe's **radius**; and for each boolean step (a cut, a join...) its **role** - **Join** (union), **Cut** (subtract), **Common** (intersect) - switch it any time, and **Separate** (that step's tool solid a positive part of its own again). Steps inside steps show indented. **Pick its curves** picks the curves it's made from, ready to drag.
+- **Ghosts:** a solid that's inside another's recipe (cutting it, joined to it, or shared with it) - or a curve with the **Cut** role inside a step - doesn't vanish: it shows where it is, see-through and drawn through the solid - **red** cutting, **green** joined, **blue** common - following every change live. Only a preview (never saved); the **Ghosts** box (by Grid / Points) turns them off.
+- **Adding tools to a solid:** the SOLID box's **Add** row - choose **Cut**, **Join** or **Common**, then **Picked curves** (the curves you've picked become a new step: extruded both ways from their plane to the solid's height - change it in the recipe) or **Other solid** (select the solid, Ctrl+click another: it becomes a new step). Each new step shows in the recipe with its own settings and role, a ghost, and Separate; one **Undo** takes it back. Add as many as you like - they nest.
+- **Roles everywhere:** every solid has a **Role** - **New solid (positive)** by default, or **Cut / Join / Common with the solid it's in** (a live boolean: the solid it's in keeps the recipe, and the role can be switched there any time). An extrusion or fill made from several curves lists **each curve with its own role**: **Add** (its outline part of the solid) or **Cut** (taken out of the others - a bite or a hole): one clean solid, made again from its curves live. In an extrusion each curve also has its own **height** and **Both ways** (the step's until you change them): a cut curve can be a shallow pocket or go right through, an added one stand taller or lower - everything that adds is built first, then everything that cuts is taken away. (With no roles set, a curve inside another is a hole, as drawn.)
+- The **CURVE** box (under CURVES) shows the picked curve's own properties: its **name**, a circle's **radius**, a line's / rectangle's / polygon's **corner radius**, **Closed** - changed at any time, live (the solids made from it follow).
+- **Moving a solid moves its curves.** A solid's place (move, turn or scale the part) is its curves' place too: they're drawn, picked, snapped and dragged where the solid is. A new solid made from them is put there as well, and copies made from them (duplicate, offset, mirror...) appear where they show.
+- One curve can drive several solids (a profile both extruded and piped), and a duplicated solid (**Shift+D**) follows the same curves - move the copy and it keeps its place while sharing the shape (the curves show with the first).
+- **Positive or negative:** a solid is **positive** (it adds) by default. While extruding, **N** makes it **negative**: the preview turns red and the hint names the solid it will cut - the one it's in - and when you click it's cut from that solid, live (reshape the curve: the pocket or hole follows). **Negative** in the SOLID box does the same to a solid already made; **Make the cut positive** (on the cut solid) gives the latest cutter back as a positive solid of its own, where it was.
+- **Live booleans:** a boolean of two solids made from curves (**Union**, **Subtract**, **Intersect** - not Slice) stays live: the result keeps the recipe "A op B" and is worked out again whenever either one's curves change (while you drag, a few times a second). B's curves show where B was. With a plain mesh on either side the result is a plain mesh.
+- It stops following its curves (a **plain mesh** from then on) when you edit its mesh in edit mode, when it's the **A** of a boolean with a plain mesh (or a Slice), or with **Make plain mesh** - **Undo** links it again. A solid whose curves are deleted stays as it was.
+- **Bake** (the SOLID box; right-click the solid in the overview or the Mesh tab's list; or the view's right-click menu, Curve modeling tab): the solid made one **Baked** solid whose **curves are its edges**. The solid as it is - its tools worked in - and every other solid touching it (overlapping or meeting it), part of it or not, become one mesh; every edge of that mesh (where its faces meet at an angle) becomes a curve - corner to corner, or a closed loop - with as few points as keep its shape (a straight edge two points, an arc three, a round rim a circle). Baking gives it a clean mesh of its own: each wall rows of quads, from each point of its bottom edge straight up to its top edge; flat faces filled from their edges (its edges kept exactly; a few thousand triangles whatever its size). Move a point of an edge - in any direction (X / Y / Z while dragging lock an axis) - and that edge of the mesh moves, the faces at it follow smoothly (every point of a face blended from the moves of the edges round it); a corner shared by several edges moves with all of them. Every edge shapes the mesh along its whole length - a wall's standing side edges too: put a point in one (double-click) and pull it, and the walls either side bend with it. While you drag, its faces follow smoothly - each wall and flat face straight between its edges, bent where a side edge bends, solved smooth across it. When you let go (or after any other edit of its curves) the solid **settles**: solved all the way, then wherever neighbouring quads bend sharply a **loop cut** runs beside that edge - every quad along the strip split in two, carried across the solid round to where it closes, so it stays quads - and that becomes its new start: the next edit bends from the shape you see, not from the bake. Undo puts the mesh back exactly. Its walls and its flat faces (tops, bottoms, a recess's ceiling) are rows and columns of quads - triangles only in the strips along curved rims. Its old curves and the solids baked in go. One undo step; saved with the model, it opens as it was.
+- The recipe is saved inside the model (in the glb) and its curves beside it: opened again, it still follows them.
+
 ## mesh-save | Saving: overrides, variants, and Revert to original | keywords: Revert to original, override, variant, Add variant, Duplicate variant, Erase variant
 - **Save** (**Ctrl+S**) never writes over the original model. In the game it saves an **override** beside it (in `art/overrides/`, laid out like the game) - the game uses your version from then on, at once (no restart, no import), and the original is kept as it was. In the [Mod Editor](doc:mod-editor) the mod's copy is the override (the game's file untouched). **Save as** (**Ctrl+Shift+S**) saves under another res:// path.
 - An override has **variants** - versions of it, numbered 1, 2, 3... The **latest is always the active one**: the game uses it. The header's variants list shows **Original** and each variant (the active one marked); pick one to open it. Saving writes into the open variant (saving the original makes a new variant).

+	"m_cv_revolve", "m_cv_loft", "m_cv_sweep", "m_cv_pipe", "m_cv_fill", "m_cv_plane"]
+
+
+static func _pts(arr: PackedVector2Array) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for q in arr:
+		out.append([q.x, q.y])
+	return out
+
+
+static func _dot(x: float, y: float) -> Dictionary:
+	return E._c(Vector2(x, y), 1.6, E.W)
+
+
+## The point a point icon is about: a bigger blue dot.
+static func _c_hi(x: float, y: float) -> Dictionary:
+	return E._c(Vector2(x, y), 2.4, E.BLUE)
+
+
+static func _bez(a: Vector2, b: Vector2, c: Vector2, d: Vector2, n := 14) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for i in n + 1:
+		var t := float(i) / n
+		var u := 1.0 - t
+		var q := a * (u * u * u) + b * (3.0 * u * u * t) + c * (3.0 * u * t * t) + d * (t * t * t)
+		out.append([q.x, q.y])
+	return out
+
+
+static func _arc(c: Vector2, r: float, a0: float, a1: float) -> Array:
+	return _pts(Icons.arc(c, r, a0, a1, 24))
+
+
+static func layers(name: String) -> Array:
+	var G := E.GOLD
+	var B := E.BLUE
+	match name:
+		"m_cv_line":   # a polyline, its corner points
+			return E._gl([[3, 16], [8, 5], [13, 13], [17, 4]], 1.6, G) + [_dot(3, 16), _dot(8, 5), _dot(13, 13), _dot(17, 4)]
+		"m_cv_wire":   # a cube's edges seen through: the wireframe
+			return E._gl([[3, 7], [12, 7], [12, 17], [3, 17], [3, 7]], 1.4, B) + E._gl([[3, 7], [8, 3], [17, 3], [12, 7]], 1.4, B) \
+				+ E._gl([[17, 3], [17, 13], [12, 17]], 1.4, B) + E._gl([[3, 12], [12, 12]], 1.0, G) + E._gl([[7.5, 7], [7.5, 17]], 1.0, G)
+		"m_cv_pt_smooth":   # a smooth bend through a point
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(2.5, 15), Vector2(7, 3), Vector2(13, 3), Vector2(17.5, 15)), 1.6, G) + [_dot(2.5, 15), _dot(17.5, 15), _c_hi(10, 6.1)]
+		"m_cv_pt_sharp":   # a corner at a point: straight either side
+			return E._gl([[2.5, 16], [10, 4], [17.5, 16]], 1.6, G) + [_dot(2.5, 16), _dot(17.5, 16), _c_hi(10, 4)]
+		"m_cv_spline":   # a smooth curve through points
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(2.5, 15), Vector2(6, 0), Vector2(13, 22), Vector2(17.5, 5)), 1.6, G) + [_dot(2.5, 15), _dot(10, 10), _dot(17.5, 5)]
+		"m_cv_circle":
+			return E._gring(Vector2(10, 10), 7.0, 1.6, G) + [_dot(10, 10), _dot(17, 10)]
+		"m_cv_arc":
+			return E._gl(_arc(Vector2(10, 13), 7.0, PI, TAU), 1.6, G) + [_dot(3, 13), _dot(10, 6), _dot(17, 13)]
+		"m_cv_rect":
+			return E._gl([[3, 5], [17, 5], [17, 15], [3, 15]], 1.6, G, true) + [_dot(3, 5), _dot(17, 15)]
+		"m_cv_polygon":
+			var p := PackedVector2Array()
+			for i in 6:
+				p.append(Vector2(10, 10) + Vector2(cos(TAU * i / 6.0), sin(TAU * i / 6.0)) * 7.5)
+			return E._gl(_pts(p), 1.6, G, true) + [_dot(10, 10)]
+		"m_cv_radial":   # copies round a centre
+			var out := [E._c(Vector2(10, 10), 1.3, E.W)]
+			for i in 6:
+				var a := TAU * i / 6.0
+				var q := Vector2(10, 10) + Vector2(cos(a), sin(a)) * 6.5
+				out.append(E._ring(q, 1.8, 1.2, G))
+			return out
+		"m_cv_offset":   # a curve and a copy beside it
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(2, 14), Vector2(6, 4), Vector2(14, 4), Vector2(18, 14)), 1.4, Color(G, 0.6)) \
+				+ E._gl(_bez(Vector2(2, 18), Vector2(6, 8), Vector2(14, 8), Vector2(18, 18)), 1.6, G) + E._arrow(Vector2(10, 7), Vector2(10, 11.5), E.W, 1.1)
+		"m_cv_fillet":   # a corner rounded
+			return [E._l([[3, 17], [3, 3], [17, 3]], 1.0, Color(E.W, 0.4))] + E._gl([[3, 17], [3, 11]] + _arc(Vector2(11, 11), 8.0, PI, PI * 1.5) + [[17, 3]], 1.6, G)
+		"m_cv_join":   # two curves meeting at a point
+			return E._gl([[2, 14], [9, 8]], 1.6, G) + E._gl([[11, 8], [18, 14]], 1.6, Color(G, 0.7)) + [E._c(Vector2(10, 8), 2.2, B)]
+		"m_cv_bridge":   # a smooth curve between two ends
+			return E._gl([[2, 16], [6, 10]], 1.6, Color(G, 0.6)) + E._gl([[14, 10], [18, 16]], 1.6, Color(G, 0.6)) \
+				+ E._gl(_bez(Vector2(6, 10), Vector2(8, 3), Vector2(12, 3), Vector2(14, 10)), 1.6, G) + [_dot(6, 10), _dot(14, 10)]
+		"m_cv_reverse":
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(3, 14), Vector2(6, 4), Vector2(14, 4), Vector2(17, 14)), 1.4, G) + E._arrow(Vector2(15, 17), Vector2(5, 17), E.W, 1.2)
+		"m_cv_close":   # an open loop with its gap closed
+			return E._gl(_arc(Vector2(10, 10), 7.0, 0.5, TAU - 0.5), 1.6, G) + [E._l([[16.1, 6.6], [16.1, 13.4]], 1.6, E.GREEN)]
+		"m_cv_extrude":   # an outline pushed up into a block
+			return [E._f([[3, 13], [12, 13], [17, 16], [8, 16]], Color(B, 0.35)), E._f([[3, 6], [12, 6], [17, 9], [8, 9]], Color(B, 0.75)),
+				E._l([[3, 6], [3, 13]], 1.0, E.W), E._l([[17, 9], [17, 16]], 1.0, E.W), E._l([[12, 6], [12, 13]], 1.0, Color(E.W, 0.5))] \
+				+ E._gl([[3, 13], [12, 13], [17, 16], [8, 16]], 1.4, G, true) + E._arrow(Vector2(10, 12), Vector2(10, 3.5), E.W, 1.2)
+		"m_cv_revolve":   # a profile turned round an axis
+			return [E._l([[10, 1.5], [10, 18.5]], 1.0, Color(E.W, 0.6)), E._f(_pts(Icons.arc(Vector2(10, 15), 7.0, 0, PI, 16)) + [[3, 15]], Color(B, 0.3))] \
+				+ E._gl([[10, 4], [15, 6], [13, 10], [16.5, 15]], 1.5, G) + E._gring(Vector2(10, 15), 6.5, 1.0, Color(E.W, 0.7), PI * 0.1, PI * 0.9)
+		"m_cv_loft":   # a skin through three rings
+			return E._gring(Vector2(10, 4.5), 4.0, 1.2, G) + E._gring(Vector2(10, 10), 6.5, 1.2, G) + E._gring(Vector2(10, 16), 3.0, 1.2, G) \
+				+ [E._l([[6, 4.5], [3.5, 10], [7, 16]], 1.0, E.W), E._l([[14, 4.5], [16.5, 10], [13, 16]], 1.0, E.W)]
+		"m_cv_sweep":   # a profile carried along a path
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(3, 17), Vector2(4, 6), Vector2(14, 14), Vector2(17, 3)), 1.1, Color(E.W, 0.8)) \
+				+ [E._f([[1, 15], [5, 15], [5, 19], [1, 19]], Color(B, 0.85)), E._f([[15, 1], [19, 1], [19, 5], [15, 5]], Color(B, 0.85))] + E._gl([[1, 15], [5, 15], [5, 19], [1, 19]], 1.0, G, true)
+		"m_cv_pipe":   # a tube along a curve
+			return E._gl(_bez(Vector2(3, 15), Vector2(5, 3), Vector2(15, 17), Vector2(17, 5)), 5.0, Color(B, 0.7)) + E._gl(_bez(Vector2(3, 15), Vector2(5, 3), Vector2(15, 17), Vector2(17, 5)), 1.0, G)
+		"m_cv_fill":   # a closed outline filled
+			return [E._f([[3, 7], [9, 3], [17, 6], [15, 16], [5, 15]], Color(B, 0.6))] + E._gl([[3, 7], [9, 3], [17, 6], [15, 16], [5, 15]], 1.4, G, true)
+		"m_cv_plane":   # a grid plane in perspective
+			return [E._f([[1, 15], [13, 15], [19, 8], [7, 8]], Color(B, 0.35)), E._l([[1, 15], [13, 15], [19, 8], [7, 8], [1, 15]], 1.2, G),
+				E._l([[4, 11.5], [16, 11.5]], 0.9, Color(E.W, 0.6)), E._l([[7, 15], [13, 8]], 0.9, Color(E.W, 0.6))]
+	return []

files.explanation: The Curve modeling tab: curves (line, spline, path, circle, arc, bezier), sketching on construction planes with snapping, editing, solids made from curves as recipes made again whenever their curves change, curve booleans, the overview and parts, baking a solid into one whose curves are its edges, and dragging points with axes and guides. A node of the mesh editor, like its other tools.

hunks.diff:
@@ -1,0 +1,7321 @@ 
+extends Node
+## The mesh editor's CURVE MODELING (its own tab on the right, and in the right-click menu): curves
+## sketched on a construction plane, then made into solids - the quick way to model hard surfaces.
+##
+## - **Curves** (the model's, kept beside it: <model file>.curves.json): a line (a polyline, its
+##   corners rounded by Fillet corners), a spline (a smooth curve through its points), a circle, a
+##   three-point arc, a bezier (a bridge, its two handles), rectangles and polygons (closed lines).
+##   Each is its control points `ctrl` in the model's own space, `closed`, the normal of its plane
+##   `n`, a line's corner radii `radii`. sample(c) turns one into points along it.
+## - **Sketching**: a tool (Line L, Spline P, Circle C, Arc Shift+C, Rectangle Shift+R, Polygon
+##   Shift+P) clicks points onto the construction plane - Auto: the surface under the first click
+##   (a face of a part: the curve drawn on it), else the ground; or Ground / Front / Side / View /
+##   the selection's. Points snap to the plane's grid and to the curves' and parts' points (Ctrl: off).
+##   Typed numbers give sizes: a length, a radius, "w h" (Enter takes them).
+## - **Editing**: a click picks a curve (Shift: more); its points dragged (snapped), the curve dragged
+##   by its line moves along its plane. Delete, duplicate, mirror, radial array, offset, fillet
+##   corners, join, reverse, close / open, bridge two ends.
+## - **Solids** (new parts, one undo step each): extrude (the mouse sets how far - or typed), revolve,
+##   loft, sweep (a profile along a path), pipe, fill (a flat face). Closed outlines make closed
+##   solids, so the booleans work on them.
+## - **Procedural**: a solid keeps its recipe on its part (meta "curve_solid": {kind, ids - its curves'
+##   ids, value - height / angle / radius, segs, axis - a revolve's axis curve}; saved in the glb's extras
+##   as "atrapos_curves") and is made again from its curves whenever they change - a point dragged, a
+##   corner filleted, an undo - or its settings do (the tab's SOLID box). Editing its mesh (edit mode) or
+##   a boolean makes it a plain mesh. Closed curves inside a closed curve are holes (extrude, fill).
+## Drawn over the view by a layer of its own (curves, handles, the plane's grid, the snap marker).
+
+const Shapes := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/shapes.gd")
+const MeshIO := preload("res://scripts/editor/mesh/mesh_io.gd")
+
+const KINDS := ["line", "spline", "circle", "arc", "bezier", "path"]
+const TOOLS := {
+	"line": ["Line", "m_cv_line", "L", "Click points on the plane: a polyline. Click its first point to close it; Enter, right-click\nor a double click ends it. Type a length + Enter for the next segment along the mouse's way."],
+	"spline": ["Spline", "m_cv_spline", "P", "Click points: a smooth curve through them. Click the first point to close it; Enter or\nright-click ends it."],
+	"circle": ["Circle", "m_cv_circle", "C", "Click the centre, then a point on the rim (or type the radius + Enter)."],
+	"arc": ["Arc", "m_cv_arc", "Shift+C", "Three points: its start, its end, then one it passes through."],
+	"rect": ["Rectangle", "m_cv_rect", "Shift+R", "Click a corner, then the opposite one (or type \"width height\" + Enter).\nAlt held: from the centre."],
+	"polygon": ["Polygon", "m_cv_polygon", "Shift+P", "Click the centre, then a corner. The wheel or + / - sets how many sides (or type the radius + Enter)."],
+}
+const PICK_PX := 9.0
+const HANDLE_PX := 10.0
+const SNAP_PX := 12.0
+const CURVE_COL := Color(0.45, 0.85, 1.0)
+const SEL_COL := Color(1.0, 0.72, 0.38)
+
+var ed: Control
+var layer: Control                 # (draws over the view)
+var curves: Array = []             # the model's curves (Dictionaries)
+var sel: Array = []                # selected curve indices, in the order picked
+var tool := ""                     # the sketching tool on ("" - none)
+var placed := PackedVector3Array() # the tool's points so far (model space)
+var cursor := Vector3.INF          # where the next point would go (snapped)
+var snap_kind := ""                # "grid", "point", "end", "mid", "centre", "vertex", "" (free)
+var typed := ""                    # numbers typed while sketching / in an operation
+var sides := 6
+## The construction plane: "auto", "ground", "front", "side", "view", "selection".
+var plane_mode := "auto"
+var plane := {}                    # {o, n, u, v} model space (the one in use)
+var grid_step := 0.05
+var snap_grid := true
+var snap_points := true
+var pipe_r := 0.05
+var segs := 32                     # (revolve / round things: steps round)
+var op := {}                       # an interactive operation (extrude / offset / fillet): its state
+var _drag := {}                    # a handle or curve being dragged
+var _cam_was := Transform3D()
+var _vertex_cache := PackedVector3Array()
+var _vertex_key := -1
+var _preview: MeshInstance3D
+var _panel_btns := {}
+var _plane_btns := {}
+var _info: Label
+var _last_click := 0
+# (The SOLID box's controls are kept in _panel_btns as "w_<name>", and the next curve id in a meta:
+# no new member variables - so a change hot reloads into an editor that's open.)
+
+
+## Each curve's placement in the model, by id: the part made from it (the first) carries it - move,
+## turn or scale a solid and its curves go with it; a live boolean's B: A's place times B's place in A.
+## Curves no solid uses aren't in it (they're where their points say).
+func owner_xfs() -> Dictionary:
+	var out := {}
+	if ed == null or ed.model == null:
+		return out
+	var inv := _mx().affine_inverse()
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+		if p.has_meta("curve_solid"):
+			_own(p.get_meta("curve_solid"), inv * p.global_transform, out)
+	return out
+
+
+static func _own(spec: Dictionary, xf: Transform3D, out: Dictionary) -> void:
+	if str(spec.get("kind", "")) == "bool":
+		_own(spec.get("a", {}), xf, out)
+		_own(spec.get("b", {}), xf * xf_of(spec.get("b_xf", [])), out)
+		return
+	for id in spec.get("ids", []) + [spec.get("axis", -1)]:
+		if int(id) >= 0 and not out.has(int(id)):
+			out[int(id)] = xf
+
+
+## Curve `c`'s placement (from owner_xfs()).
+static func cx(c: Dictionary, own: Dictionary) -> Transform3D:
+	return own.get(int(c.get("id", -1)), Transform3D())
+
+
+## A copy of `c` with its placement put into its points (a copy made from a placed curve: where it shows).
+static func baked(c: Dictionary, x: Transform3D) -> Dictionary:
+	var o := c.duplicate(true)
+	if x == Transform3D():
+		return o
+	var k: PackedVector3Array = (o["ctrl"] as PackedVector3Array).duplicate()
+	for j in k.size():
+		k[j] = x * k[j]
+	o["ctrl"] = k
+	o["n"] = (x.basis * (c.get("n", Vector3.UP) as Vector3)).normalized()
+	return o
+
+
+## A transform as 12 numbers (JSON, the glb's extras) and back.
+static func xf_arr(t: Transform3D) -> Array:
+	return [t.basis.x.x, t.basis.x.y, t.basis.x.z, t.basis.y.x, t.basis.y.y, t.basis.y.z, t.basis.z.x, t.basis.z.y, t.basis.z.z, t.origin.x, t.origin.y, t.origin.z]
+
+
+static func xf_of(a: Variant) -> Transform3D:
+	if not a is Array or (a as Array).size() < 12:
+		return Transform3D()
+	return Transform3D(Basis(Vector3(a[0], a[1], a[2]), Vector3(a[3], a[4], a[5]), Vector3(a[6], a[7], a[8])), Vector3(a[9], a[10], a[11]))
+
+
+## The next id a curve gets (each curve's id: what a solid's recipe names it by).
+func _nid() -> int:
+	return int(get_meta("next_curve_id", 1))
+
+
+func _set_nid(n: int) -> void:
+	set_meta("next_curve_id", n)
+
+
+## A control of the SOLID box (null: not built).
+func _w(k: String) -> Variant:
+	var c = _panel_btns.get("w_" + k)
+	return c if c != null and is_instance_valid(c) else null
+
+
+func setup(editor: Control) -> void:
+	ed = editor
+	name = "CurveTools"
+
+
+## The overlay, once the view is made.
+func attach(view: Control) -> void:
+	layer = Control.new()
+	layer.name = "CurveLayer"
+	layer.mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
+	layer.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
+	layer.draw.connect(_draw_layer)
+	view.add_child(layer)
+
+
+func _process(_dt: float) -> void:
+	if layer == null or ed.view == null or ed.view.cam == null:
+		return
+	if has_meta("solids_pending") and Time.get_ticks_msec() - int(get_meta("bool_at", 0)) >= 120:
+		remove_meta("solids_pending")
+		refresh_solids()
+	var t: Transform3D = ed.view.cam.global_transform
+	if t != _cam_was:
+		_cam_was = t
+		if not curves.is_empty() or tool != "":
+			layer.queue_redraw()
+	# (a solid carrying curves moved - G, the gizmo, a drag, typed numbers: its curves drawn with it at once)
+	if not curves.is_empty() and ed.model:
+		var sig := 0
+		for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+			if p.has_meta("curve_solid"):
+				sig = hash([sig, p.transform])
+		if sig != int(get_meta("placed_sig", 0)):
+			set_meta("placed_sig", sig)
+			layer.queue_redraw()
+	# (the ghosts of the solids inside recipes: made again when a recipe, a place or a part's showing changes)
+	var gs := ghost_sig()
+	if gs != int(get_meta("ghost_sig", 0)):
+		set_meta("ghost_sig", gs)
+		update_ghosts()
+
+
+func _exit_tree() -> void:
+	# (a baked solid's weights still being worked out on a worker: waited for - never left running)
+	if has_meta("edge_bases"):
+		for k in (get_meta("edge_bases") as Dictionary):
+			var c = get_meta("edge_bases")[k]
+			if c is Dictionary and (c as Dictionary).has("bw_job"):
+				WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion(int(c["bw_job"][0]))
+				(c as Dictionary).erase("bw_job")
+
+
+func active() -> bool:
+	return tool != "" or not op.is_empty() or not _drag.is_empty()
+
+
+# --- the curves' shapes (static: tests call them) ---------------------------------------
+
+## Points along curve `c` (model space): a line's corners (rounded by its radii), a spline through
+## its points, a circle, an arc, a bezier.
+static func sample(c: Dictionary, per := 12) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var k: PackedVector3Array = c["ctrl"]
+	var closed: bool = c.get("closed", false)
+	match str(c["kind"]):
+		"line":
+			return _rounded(k, c.get("radii", PackedFloat32Array()), closed, c.get("n", Vector3.UP))
+		"spline":
+			return catmull(k, closed, per)
+		"path":
+			return path_pts(k, c.get("sharp", PackedByteArray()), closed, per)
+		"circle":
+			if k.size() < 2:
+				return k.duplicate()
+			return circle_pts(k[0], k[0].distance_to(k[1]), c.get("n", Vector3.UP), k[1] - k[0], 64)
+		"arc":
+			return arc3(k[0], k[2], k[1], 48) if k.size() >= 3 else k.duplicate()
+		"bezier":
+			var out := PackedVector3Array()
+			if k.size() < 4:
+				return k.duplicate()
+			for i in 33:
+				var t := i / 32.0
+				var u := 1.0 - t
+				out.append(k[0] * (u * u * u) + k[1] * (3.0 * u * u * t) + k[2] * (3.0 * u * t * t) + k[3] * (t * t * t))
+			return out
+	return k.duplicate()
+
+
+## A path: a curve through its points, smooth through most, broken at the `sharp` ones (corners):
+## between two corners a smooth run (a spline through the points between) or, with none between, a
+## straight side. (What a boolean of curves leaves: straight sides and arcs with few points.)
+static func path_pts(k: PackedVector3Array, sharp: PackedByteArray, closed: bool, per := 12) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var n := k.size()
+	var corners := PackedInt32Array()
+	for i in n:
+		if (i < sharp.size() and sharp[i] == 1) or (not closed and (i == 0 or i == n - 1)):
+			corners.append(i)
+	if corners.is_empty():
+		return catmull(k, closed, per)
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	var cn := corners.size()
+	var runs := cn if closed else cn - 1
+	for r in runs:
+		var a := corners[r]
+		var b := corners[(r + 1) % cn]
+		var piece := PackedVector3Array()
+		var j := a
+		while true:
+			piece.append(k[j])
+			if j == b and piece.size() > 1:
+				break
+			j = (j + 1) % n
+			if piece.size() > n + 1:
+				break
+		if piece.size() <= 2:
+			out.append(piece[0])   # (a straight side: its corner)
+		else:
+			var arc := _arc_run(piece)   # (its points on one circle - a boolean's arc: drawn exactly)
+			var sp := arc if not arc.is_empty() else catmull(piece, false, per)
+			sp.remove_at(sp.size() - 1)
+			out.append_array(sp)
+	if not closed:
+		out.append(k[n - 1])
+	return out
+
+
+## A centripetal Catmull-Rom spline through `k` (`per` points a span).
+static func catmull(k: PackedVector3Array, closed: bool, per := 12) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var n := k.size()
+	if n < 3:
+		return k.duplicate()
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	var spans := n if closed else n - 1
+	for s in spans:
+		var p1 := k[s]
+		var p2 := k[(s + 1) % n]
+		# (an open end: a point beyond it carrying on the bend of the last three - an arc stays round
+		# to its end, not straightened)
+		var p0 := k[(s - 1 + n) % n] if (closed or s > 0) else _beyond(k[0], k[1], k[2])
+		var p3 := k[(s + 2) % n] if (closed or s + 2 < n) else _beyond(k[n - 1], k[n - 2], k[n - 3])
+		var t0 := 0.0
+		var t1 := t0 + maxf(sqrt(p0.distance_to(p1)), 1e-4)
+		var t2 := t1 + maxf(sqrt(p1.distance_to(p2)), 1e-4)
+		var t3 := t2 + maxf(sqrt(p2.distance_to(p3)), 1e-4)
+		for i in per:
+			var t := lerpf(t1, t2, float(i) / per)
+			var a1 := p0 * ((t1 - t) / (t1 - t0)) + p1 * ((t - t0) / (t1 - t0))
+			var a2 := p1 * ((t2 - t) / (t2 - t1)) + p2 * ((t - t1) / (t2 - t1))
+			var a3 := p2 * ((t3 - t) / (t3 - t2)) + p3 * ((t - t2) / (t3 - t2))
+			var b1 := a1 * ((t2 - t) / (t2 - t0)) + a2 * ((t - t0) / (t2 - t0))
+			var b2 := a2 * ((t3 - t) / (t3 - t1)) + a3 * ((t - t1) / (t3 - t1))
+			out.append(b1 * ((t2 - t) / (t2 - t1)) + b2 * ((t - t1) / (t2 - t1)))
+	if not closed:
+		out.append(k[n - 1])
+	return out
+
+
+## The run of points `piece` as an exact arc when they all lie on one circle (through its ends and
+## middle point; [] - they don't: a spline then).
+static func _arc_run(piece: PackedVector3Array) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var a := piece[0]
+	var b := piece[piece.size() - 1]
+	var mid := piece[piece.size() / 2]
+	var ctr := circumcentre(a, mid, b)
+	if ctr == Vector3.INF:
+		return PackedVector3Array()
+	var r := a.distance_to(ctr)
+	var tol := maxf(r * 4e-3, 1e-5)   # (a boolean's corners lie on the outline's straight sides: up to ~0.12% of r inside the circle)
+	var nn := (mid - a).cross(b - a)
+	for q in piece:
+		if absf(q.distance_to(ctr) - r) > tol or absf((q - a).dot(nn.normalized())) > tol:
+			return PackedVector3Array()
+	var ang := (a - ctr).angle_to(mid - ctr) + (mid - ctr).angle_to(b - ctr)
+	return arc3(a, b, mid, maxi(4, int(ceil(rad_to_deg(ang) / 4.0))))
+
+
+## A point beyond end `a` carrying on the bend of `a`, `b`, `c` (the circle through them, as far
+## before `a` as `b` is after it; in a row: straight on).
+static func _beyond(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3) -> Vector3:
+	var ctr := circumcentre(a, b, c)
+	var nn := (b - a).cross(c - a)
+	if ctr == Vector3.INF or nn.length() < 1e-12:
+		return a * 2.0 - b
+	nn = nn.normalized()
+	var ang := (a - ctr).signed_angle_to(b - ctr, nn)
+	return ctr + (a - ctr).rotated(nn, -ang)
+
+
+## A circle round `c` of radius `r` in the plane facing `n`, starting towards `start`.
+static func circle_pts(c: Vector3, r: float, n: Vector3, start: Vector3, count := 64) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var nn := n.normalized()
+	var u := (start - nn * start.dot(nn))
+	u = u.normalized() if u.length() > 1e-6 else _any_perp(nn)
+	var v := nn.cross(u)
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	for i in count:
+		var a := TAU * i / count
+		out.append(c + (u * cos(a) + v * sin(a)) * r)
+	return out
+
+
+## The arc from `a` to `b` through `m` (a straight line if the three are in a row).
+static func arc3(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, m: Vector3, count := 48) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var ctr := circumcentre(a, m, b)
+	if ctr == Vector3.INF:
+		return PackedVector3Array([a, b])
+	var n := (m - a).cross(b - a).normalized()
+	var u := (a - ctr).normalized()
+	var v := n.cross(u)
+	var r := a.distance_to(ctr)
+	var ang_b := fposmod(atan2((b - ctr).dot(v), (b - ctr).dot(u)), TAU)
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	for i in count + 1:
+		var t := ang_b * i / count
+		out.append(ctr + (u * cos(t) + v * sin(t)) * r)
+	return out
+
+
+## The centre of the circle through three points (INF: they're in a row).
+static func circumcentre(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, c: Vector3) -> Vector3:
+	var ab := b - a
+	var ac := c - a
+	var n := ab.cross(ac)
+	var d := 2.0 * n.length_squared()
+	if d < 1e-12:
+		return Vector3.INF
+	return a + (n.cross(ab) * ac.length_squared() + ac.cross(n) * ab.length_squared()) / d
+
+
+static func _any_perp(n: Vector3) -> Vector3:
+	var a := Vector3.UP if absf(n.y) < 0.9 else Vector3.RIGHT
+	return n.cross(a).normalized()
+
+
+## A polyline with its corners rounded: corner i by radii[i] (an arc tangent to both sides).
+static func _rounded(k: PackedVector3Array, radii: PackedFloat32Array, closed: bool, n: Vector3) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var m := k.size()
+	if radii.is_empty() or m < 3:
+		return k.duplicate()   # (a copy: callers turn it round - never the curve's own points)
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	for i in m:
+		var r := radii[i] if i < radii.size() else 0.0
+		var ends := (i == 0 or i == m - 1) and not closed
+		if r <= 1e-6 or ends:
+			out.append(k[i])
+			continue
+		var p := k[i]
+		var a := k[(i - 1 + m) % m]
+		var b := k[(i + 1) % m]
+		var da := (a - p).normalized()
+		var db := (b - p).normalized()
+		var cosang := clampf(da.dot(db), -1.0, 1.0)
+		var half := acos(cosang) * 0.5
+		if half < 1e-3 or half > PI * 0.5 - 1e-3:
+			out.append(p)
+			continue
+		# (the tangent points: as far back as the radius needs, no further than half a side)
+		var back := r / tan(half)
+		var lim := minf(p.distance_to(a), p.distance_to(b)) * 0.5
+		if back > lim:
+			back = lim
+			r = back * tan(half)
+		if r < 1e-6 or (da + db).length() < 1e-6:
+			out.append(p)   # (a point on top of its neighbour, or no room: left sharp)
+			continue
+		var t0 := p + da * back
+		var t1 := p + db * back
+		var ctr := p + (da + db).normalized() * (r / sin(half))
+		var steps := maxi(3, int(ceil((PI - 2.0 * half) / deg_to_rad(10.0))))
+		var u := (t0 - ctr).normalized()
+		var ax := (t0 - ctr).cross(t1 - ctr).normalized()
+		var sweep := (PI - 2.0 * half)
+		for s in steps + 1:
+			out.append(ctr + u.rotated(ax, sweep * s / steps) * r)
+	return out
+
+
+# --- the construction plane ----------------------------------------------------------------
+
+static func plane_of(mode: String, cam_basis := Basis()) -> Dictionary:
+	match mode:
+		"front": return _plane(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.BACK, Vector3.RIGHT)
+		"side": return _plane(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.RIGHT, Vector3.BACK * -1.0)
+		"view": return _plane(Vector3.ZERO, cam_basis.z, cam_basis.x)
+	return _plane(Vector3.ZERO, Vector3.UP, Vector3.RIGHT)
+
+
+static func _plane(o: Vector3, n: Vector3, u: Vector3) -> Dictionary:
+	n = n.normalized()
+	u = (u - n * u.dot(n))
+	u = u.normalized() if u.length() > 1e-6 else _any_perp(n)
+	return {"o": o, "n": n, "u": u, "v": n.cross(u)}
+
+
+## The model's transform (model space <-> the view's world).
+func _mx() -> Transform3D:
+	return ed.model.global_transform if ed.model else Transform3D()
+
+
+## The plane for a new sketch from the mouse at `at`: Auto - the part's surface under it.
+func _plane_for(at: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
+	if plane_mode == "auto":
+		var hit := _surface_hit(at)
+		if not hit.is_empty():
+			return _plane(hit["p"], hit["n"], Vector3.RIGHT if absf(hit["n"].x) < 0.9 else Vector3.BACK)
+		return plane_of("ground")
+	if plane_mode == "view":
+		return plane_of("view", _mx().basis.inverse() * ed.view.cam.global_basis)
+	if plane_mode == "selection":
+		var p := selection_plane()
+		return p if not p.is_empty() else plane_of("ground")
+	return plane_of(plane_mode)
+
+
+## The selection's plane: the selected faces' (edit mode), else the first selected curve's.
+func selection_plane() -> Dictionary:
+	if ed.mode == "edit" and ed.em != null and ed.part != null:
+		var ids: PackedInt32Array = ed.selected_points()
+		if ids.size() >= 3:
+			var DT: GDScript = load("res://scripts/editor/mesh/deform_tools.gd")
+			var n: Vector3 = DT.faces_normal(ed.em, ed.sel_t) if ed.sel_kind != 0 else Vector3.ZERO
+			if n == Vector3.ZERO:
+				n = DT.fit_normal(ed.em.points, ids)
+			var pxf: Transform3D = _mx().affine_inverse() * ed.part.global_transform
+			var c: Vector3 = pxf * ed.em.centroid(ids)
+			return _plane(c, (pxf.basis * n).normalized(), Vector3.RIGHT if absf(n.x) < 0.9 else Vector3.BACK)
+	if not sel.is_empty():
+		var c := baked(curves[sel[0]], cx(curves[sel[0]], owner_xfs()))
+		var k: PackedVector3Array = c["ctrl"]
+		return _plane(k[0], c.get("n", Vector3.UP), (k[1] - k[0]) if k.size() > 1 else Vector3.RIGHT)
+	return {}
+
+
+## A part's surface under the mouse: {p, n} in model space ({} - none).
+func _surface_hit(at: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
+	var r: Array = ed.view.ray(at)
+	var best := INF
+	var out := {}
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+		if not p.visible or p.mesh == null:
+			continue
+		var tm := p.mesh.generate_triangle_mesh()
+		if tm == null:
+			continue
+		var inv := p.global_transform.affine_inverse()
+		var o: Vector3 = inv * (r[0] as Vector3)
+		var d: Vector3 = (inv.basis * (r[1] as Vector3)).normalized()
+		var hit := tm.intersect_ray(o, d)
+		if hit.is_empty():
+			continue
+		var wp: Vector3 = p.global_transform * (hit["position"] as Vector3)
+		var dist := wp.distance_to(r[0])
+		if dist < best:
+			best = dist
+			var mi := _mx().affine_inverse()
+			var wn: Vector3 = (p.global_transform.basis.inverse().transposed() * (hit["normal"] as Vector3)).normalized()
+			out = {"p": mi * wp, "n": (mi.basis * wn).normalized()}
+	return out
+
+
+## The mouse on plane `pl` (model space), INF if the plane's edge-on.
+func _on_plane(at: Vector2, pl: Dictionary) -> Vector3:
+	var mx := _mx()
+	var hit = ed.view.on_plane(at, mx * (pl["o"] as Vector3), (mx.basis * (pl["n"] as Vector3)).normalized())
+	return mx.affine_inverse() * (hit as Vector3) if hit != null else Vector3.INF
+
+
+func _screen(p: Vector3) -> Vector2:
+	var w := _mx() * p
+	return Vector2(-1e6, -1e6) if ed.view.behind(w) else ed.view.project(w)
+
+
+## Where a point goes for the mouse at `at` on plane `pl`: a curve's or part's point near it, else
+## the grid (Ctrl: free). Sets snap_kind.
+func snap(at: Vector2, pl: Dictionary, free := false) -> Vector3:
+	var p := _on_plane(at, pl)
+	snap_kind = ""
+	if p == Vector3.INF or free:
+		return p
+	if snap_points:
+		var best := SNAP_PX
+		var got := Vector3.INF
+		for cand in _snap_candidates():
+			var d := _screen(cand[0]).distance_to(at)
+			if d < best:
+				best = d
+				got = cand[0]
+				snap_kind = cand[1]
+		if got != Vector3.INF:
+			return got
+	if snap_grid and grid_step > 0.0:
+		var o: Vector3 = pl["o"]
+		var u: Vector3 = pl["u"]
+		var v: Vector3 = pl["v"]
+		var a := snappedf((p - o).dot(u), grid_step)
+		var b := snappedf((p - o).dot(v), grid_step)
+		snap_kind = "grid"
+		return o + u * a + v * b
+	return p
+
+
+## Points to snap to: [model-space point, kind].
+func _snap_candidates() -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	var own := owner_xfs()
+	for c0 in curves:
+		if c0.get("hidden", false):
+			continue
+		var c := baked(c0, cx(c0, own))
+		var k: PackedVector3Array = c["ctrl"]
+		match str(c["kind"]):
+			"circle":
+				out.append([k[0], "centre"])
+				for q in circle_pts(k[0], k[0].distance_to(k[1]), c["n"], k[1] - k[0], 4):
+					out.append([q, "point"])
+			_:
+				var s := sample(c)
+				if not s.is_empty() and not c.get("closed", false):
+					out.append([s[0], "end"])
+					out.append([s[s.size() - 1], "end"])
+				for i in k.size():
+					out.append([k[i], "point"])
+					if str(c["kind"]) == "line" and (i + 1 < k.size() or c.get("closed", false)):
+						out.append([(k[i] + k[(i + 1) % k.size()]) * 0.5, "mid"])
+	for q in placed:
+		out.append([q, "point"])
+	for q in _part_vertices():
+		out.append([q, "vertex"])
+	return out
+
+
+## The visible parts' corner points (model space; kept till the model changes) - at most a few thousand.
+func _part_vertices() -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var key: int = ed._edit_count * 7919 + ed.parts().size() * 31 + (ed._undo.size() as int)
+	if key == _vertex_key:
+		return _vertex_cache
+	_vertex_key = key
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	var seen := {}
+	var mi := _mx().affine_inverse()
+	for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+		if not p.visible or p.mesh == null:
+			continue
+		var xf := mi * p.global_transform
+		var fs := p.mesh.get_faces()
+		if fs.size() > 12000:
+			continue
+		for q in fs:
+			var w := xf * q
+			var kk := Vector3i((w * 1000.0).round())
+			if not seen.has(kk):
+				seen[kk] = true
+				out.append(w)
+	_vertex_cache = out
+	return out
+
+
+# --- sketching ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func begin(t: String) -> void:
+	if not TOOLS.has(t):
+		return
+	cancel_op()
+	if ed.model == null:
+		ed.new_model(true)
+	tool = t
+	placed = PackedVector3Array()
+	typed = ""
+	plane = {}
+	cursor = Vector3.INF
+	ed.show_right_tab(1)
+	_hint()
+	_refresh_panel()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+
+
+func stop() -> void:
+	tool = ""
+	placed = PackedVector3Array()
+	typed = ""
+	plane = {}
+	ed.view.hint = ""
+	ed.view.queue_redraw()
+	_refresh_panel()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+
+
+func _hint() -> void:
+	if tool == "":
+		return
+	var t: Array = TOOLS[tool]
+	var what := ""
+	match tool:
+		"line", "spline": what = "click points · Enter / right-click: done · click the first: closed · Backspace: back"
+		"circle": what = "centre, then the rim" if placed.is_empty() else "the rim (or type the radius)"
+		"arc": what = ["its start", "its end", "a point it passes through"][mini(placed.size(), 2)]
+		"rect": what = "a corner" if placed.is_empty() else "the opposite corner (or type \"w h\")"
+		"polygon": what = ("the centre" if placed.is_empty() else "a corner (or type the radius)") + " · %d sides (wheel / + -)" % sides
+	var pl: String = ["Auto", "Ground", "Front", "Side", "View", "Selection"][["auto", "ground", "front", "side", "view", "selection"].find(plane_mode)]
+	ed.view.hint = "%s:  %s   [%s plane%s]%s" % [t[0], what, pl, "" if snap_kind == "" else " · snap: " + snap_kind, ("   typed: " + typed) if typed != "" else ""]
+	ed.view.queue_redraw()
+
+
+## A sketch click at `at` (`free`: no snapping). True - taken.
+func click(at: Vector2, free := false) -> bool:
+	if tool == "":
+		return false
+	if plane.is_empty():
+		plane = _plane_for(at)
+	var p := snap(at, plane, free)
+	if p == Vector3.INF:
+		ed._say("The construction plane is edge-on: turn the view a little.")
+		return true
+	var now := Time.get_ticks_msec()
+	# (a double click: quick, and on the point just placed)
+	var dbl := now - _last_click < 300 and not placed.is_empty() and _screen(placed[placed.size() - 1]).distance_to(at) < SNAP_PX
+	_last_click = now
+	match tool:
+		"line", "spline":
+			if placed.size() >= 3 and _screen(placed[0]).distance_to(at) < SNAP_PX:
+				_finish(true)
+				return true
+			if dbl and placed.size() >= 2:
+				_finish(false)
+				return true
+			if placed.is_empty() or placed[placed.size() - 1].distance_to(p) > 1e-6:
+				placed.append(p)
+		"circle":
+			placed.append(p)
+			if placed.size() == 2:
+				_finish(true)
+		"arc":
+			placed.append(p)
+			if placed.size() == 3:
+				_finish(false)
+		"rect":
+			placed.append(p)
+			if placed.size() == 2:
+				_finish(true)
+		"polygon":
+			placed.append(p)
+			if placed.size() == 2:
+				_finish(true)
+	_hint()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+	return true
+
+
+## The curve sketched so far for the tool (with the cursor as its next point).
+func _draft() -> Dictionary:
+	var pts := placed.duplicate()
+	if cursor != Vector3.INF:
+		pts.append(cursor)
+	var n: Vector3 = plane.get("n", Vector3.UP)
+	match tool:
+		"line": return {"kind": "line", "ctrl": pts, "closed": false, "n": n}
+		"spline": return {"kind": "spline", "ctrl": pts, "closed": false, "n": n}
+		"circle":
+			return {"kind": "circle", "ctrl": pts, "closed": true, "n": n} if pts.size() >= 2 else {}
+		"arc":
+			if pts.size() == 2:
+				return {"kind": "line", "ctrl": pts, "closed": false, "n": n}
+			if pts.size() >= 3:
+				return {"kind": "arc", "ctrl": PackedVector3Array([pts[0], pts[2], pts[1]]), "closed": false, "n": n}
+			return {}
+		"rect":
+			if pts.size() < 2:
+				return {}
+			return {"kind": "line", "ctrl": rect_pts(pts[0], pts[1], plane, Input.is_key_pressed(KEY_ALT)), "closed": true, "n": n}
+		"polygon":
+			if pts.size() < 2:
+				return {}
+			return {"kind": "line", "ctrl": polygon_pts(pts[0], pts[1], n, sides), "closed": true, "n": n}
+	return {}
+
+
+## A rectangle's corners from `a` to `b` on plane `pl` (`centred`: `a` is its middle).
+static func rect_pts(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, pl: Dictionary, centred := false) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var u: Vector3 = pl.get("u", Vector3.RIGHT)
+	var v: Vector3 = pl.get("v", Vector3.BACK)
+	var d := b - a
+	var du := u * d.dot(u)
+	var dv := v * d.dot(v)
+	if centred:
+		return PackedVector3Array([a - du - dv, a + du - dv, a + du + dv, a - du + dv])
+	return PackedVector3Array([a, a + du, a + du + dv, a + dv])
+
+
+## A regular polygon's corners round `c`, one of them at `corner`.
+static func polygon_pts(c: Vector3, corner: Vector3, n: Vector3, count: int) -> PackedVector3Array:
+	var out := PackedVector3Array()
+	var r := corner - c
+	for i in count:
+		out.append(c + r.rotated(n.normalized(), TAU * i / count))
+	return out
+
+
+func _finish(closed: bool) -> void:
+	var save_cursor := cursor
+	cursor = Vector3.INF
+	var c := _draft()
+	cursor = save_cursor
+	if tool in ["line", "spline"]:
+		if placed.size() < 2:
+			stop()
+			return
+		c["closed"] = closed and placed.size() >= 3
+	if c.is_empty():
+		stop()
+		return
+	var kept_tool := tool
+	add_curve(c)
+	placed = PackedVector3Array()
+	plane = {} if plane_mode in ["auto", "view"] else plane
+	typed = ""
+	tool = kept_tool   # (the tool stays on: another one, at once - Esc stops it)
+	_hint()
+
+
+## Adds curve `c` (one undo step); its index.
+func add_curve(c: Dictionary) -> int:
+	c = c.duplicate(true)
+	_fresh(c)
+	if not c.has("name"):
+		c["name"] = "%s %d" % [str(c["kind"]).capitalize(), curves.size() + 1]
+	var before := _state()
+	curves.append(c)
+	sel = [curves.size() - 1]
+	_changed("Add " + str(c["kind"]), before)
+	return curves.size() - 1
+
+
+## `c` given an id of its own (a new curve, or a copy).
+func _fresh(c: Dictionary) -> Dictionary:
+	c["id"] = _nid()
+	_set_nid(_nid() + 1)
+	return c
+
+
+## The curve with id `id` ({} - none).
+func curve_by_id(id: int) -> Dictionary:
+	for c in curves:
+		if int(c.get("id", -1)) == id:
+			return c
+	return {}
+
+
+## The curves with these ids, in order ([] if one of them is gone).
+func curves_of(ids: Array) -> Array:
+	var out := []
+	for id in ids:
+		var c := curve_by_id(int(id))
+		if c.is_empty():
+			return []
+		out.append(c)
+	return out
+
+
+## Typed numbers while sketching: a length / radius / "w h".
+func apply_typed() -> bool:
+	var nums := []
+	for s in typed.replace(",", " ").split(" ", false):
+		if s.is_valid_float():
+			nums.append(float(s))
+	typed = ""
+	if nums.is_empty() or placed.is_empty():
+		return false
+	var a := placed[placed.size() - 1]
+	var dir: Vector3 = (cursor - a) if cursor != Vector3.INF else plane.get("u", Vector3.RIGHT)
+	if dir.length() < 1e-6:
+		dir = plane.get("u", Vector3.RIGHT)
+	dir = dir.normalized()
+	match tool:
+		"line", "spline":
+			placed.append(a + dir * nums[0])
+		"circle", "polygon":
+			cursor = Vector3.INF
+			placed.append(a + dir * nums[0])
+			_finish(true)
+		"rect":
+			var u: Vector3 = plane["u"]
+			var v: Vector3 = plane["v"]
+			var sx := signf((cursor - a).dot(u)) if cursor != Vector3.INF and absf((cursor - a).dot(u)) > 1e-6 else 1.0
+			var sy := signf((cursor - a).dot(v)) if cursor != Vector3.INF and absf((cursor - a).dot(v)) > 1e-6 else 1.0
+			cursor = Vector3.INF
+			placed.append(a + u * nums[0] * sx + v * (nums[1] if nums.size() > 1 else nums[0]) * sy)
+			_finish(true)
+	_hint()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+	return true
+
+
+# --- undo -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+func _state() -> Array:
+	# (baked solids' recipes too: an edit settles their meshes - undo puts each back as it was)
+	var specs := {}
+	if ed and ed.model:
+		for p: MeshInstance3D in ed.parts():
+			var sp: Dictionary = p.get_meta("curve_solid", {})
+			if str(sp.get("kind", "")) == "edges" and sp.has("mesh"):
+				specs[p.get_instance_id()] = sp.duplicate(true)
+	return [curves.duplicate(true), sel.duplicate(), specs]
+
+
+func _set_state(st: Array) -> void:
+	curves = st[0].duplicate(true)
+	sel = st[1].duplicate()
+	if st.size() > 2:
+		for pid in st[2]:
+			var p = instance_from_id(int(pid))
+			if p is MeshInstance3D and is_instance_valid(p):
+				var sp: Dictionary = (st[2][pid] as Dictionary).duplicate(true)
+				(p as MeshInstance3D).set_meta("curve_solid", sp)
+				(p as MeshInstance3D).remove_meta("curve_solid_key")
+				_edge_bases().erase(int(sp.get("net", 0)))
+	refresh_solids()
+	_refresh_panel()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+
+
+## One undo step from `before` to now (a baked solid an edit reshaped: settled first - in the step).
+func _changed(name: String, before: Array) -> void:
+	refresh_solids()
+	settle_edges()
+	var after := _state()
+	var e := {"name": name, "undo": _set_state.bind(before), "redo": _set_state.bind(after)}
+	if ed.mode == "edit":
+		ed._eundo.append(e)
+		ed._eredo.clear()
+		ed.dirty = true
+		ed._update_ui()
+	else:
+		ed._push(name, _set_state.bind(before), _set_state.bind(after))
+	refresh_solids()
+	_refresh_panel()
+	layer.queue_redraw()
+
+
+# --- picking and dragging ----------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+## The curve whose line passes nearest `at` (-1: none within PICK_PX; a run behind the solid isn't picked).
+func pick(at: Vector2) -> int:
+	return int(pick_at(at).get("i", -1))
+
+
+## pick()'s curve and where on it: {i, p - the point (the curve's own space)} ({}: none).
+func pick_at(at: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
+	var best := PICK_PX
+	var got := {}
+	var own := owner_xfs()
+	var mx := _mx()
+	_begin_occ(false)
+	for i in curves.size():
+		if curves[i].get("hidden", false):
+			continue
+		var s := sample(curves[i])
+		var x := cx(curves[i], own)
+		if curves[i].get("closed", false) and s.size() > 1:
+			s.append(s[0])
+		for k in s.size() - 1:
+			var a := _screen(x * s[k])
+			var b := _screen(x * s[k + 1])
+			var q := Geometry2D.get_closest_point_to_segment(at, a, b)
+			var d := q.distance_to(at)
+			if d < best:
+				var ab := b - a
+				var t := clampf((q - a).dot(ab) / ab.length_squared(), 0.0, 1.0) if ab.length_squared() > 1e-9 else 0.0
+				var p := s[k].lerp(s[k + 1], t)
+				if _hidden(mx * (x * p)):
+					continue
+				best = d
+				got = {"i": i, "p": p}
+	_end_occ()
+	return got
+
+
+## Double-click on a curve: a point put into it there (a circle, an arc or a bezier becomes a path of
+## points first - the same shape). False: not one to add to.
+func insert_point(at: Vector2) -> bool:
+	var hit := pick_at(at)
+	if hit.is_empty():
+		return false
+	var i := int(hit["i"])
+	var c: Dictionary = curves[i]
+	var p: Vector3 = hit["p"]
+	var before := _state()
+	var e := as_points(c)
+	if e.is_empty():
+		return false
+	if str(c["kind"]) in ["circle"]:
+		var k0: PackedVector3Array = c["ctrl"]
+		var n := (c.get("n", Vector3.UP) as Vector3).normalized()
+		var off := p - k0[0]
+		off -= n * off.dot(n)
+		if off.length() > 1e-9:
+			p = k0[0] + off.normalized() * k0[0].distance_to(k0[1])   # (exactly on the circle)
+	var k: PackedVector3Array = e["ctrl"]
+	var closed: bool = e.get("closed", false)
+	var spans := k.size() if closed else k.size() - 1
+	var at_j := -1
+	var cost := INF
+	for j in spans:
+		var a := k[j]
+		var b := k[(j + 1) % k.size()]
+		var dc := a.distance_to(p) + p.distance_to(b) - a.distance_to(b)   # (the detour: least where it lies between them)
+		if dc < cost:
+			cost = dc
+			at_j = j
+	if at_j < 0:
+		return false
+	for q in k:
+		if q.distance_to(p) < 1e-4:
+			return false   # (a point's already there)
+	k.insert(at_j + 1, p)
+	e["ctrl"] = k
+	if e.has("radii"):
+		var r: PackedFloat32Array = e["radii"]
+		if r.size() >= at_j + 1:
+			r.insert(at_j + 1, 0.0)
+		e["radii"] = r
+	if str(e["kind"]) == "path":
+		var sh: PackedByteArray = e.get("sharp", PackedByteArray())
+		sh.resize(k.size() - 1)
+		sh.insert(at_j + 1, 0)
+		e["sharp"] = sh
+	curves[i] = e
+	if not i in sel:
+		sel = [i]
+	_changed("Insert curve point", before)
+	return true
+
+
+## Double-click on a point: it's taken out - the curve runs on between its neighbours (an arc's middle
+## point: a straight line between its ends). Not when that leaves too few (2 for an open curve, 3 for a
+## closed one), nor a baked solid's edge end (a corner other edges share). One undo step.
+func dissolve_point(ci: int, j: int) -> bool:
+	if ci < 0 or ci >= curves.size():
+		return false
+	var c: Dictionary = curves[ci]
+	var k: PackedVector3Array = c["ctrl"]
+	var closed := bool(c.get("closed", false))
+	var kind := str(c["kind"])
+	var e := c.duplicate(true)
+	if kind == "arc":
+		if j != 1 or k.size() < 3:
+			return false
+		e["kind"] = "line"
+		e["ctrl"] = PackedVector3Array([k[0], k[2]])
+	elif kind in ["line", "spline", "path"]:
+		if k.size() <= (3 if closed else 2) or j < 0 or j >= k.size():
+			return false
+		if not closed and (j == 0 or j == k.size() - 1) and _any_baked([ci]):
+			return false
+		var nk := k.duplicate()
+		nk.remove_at(j)
+		e["ctrl"] = nk
+		for key_ in ["sharp", "radii"]:
+			if e.has(key_):
+				var a = e[key_]
+				if j < a.size():
+					a.remove_at(j)
+				e[key_] = a
+	else:
+		return false
+	var before := _state()
+	curves[ci] = e
+	_changed("Dissolve curve point", before)
+	return true
+
+
+## The menu's items for a picked curve's point under `at` - Smooth point / Sharp point ([]: none there).
+func point_items(at: Vector2) -> Array:
+	var h := pick_handle(at) if at.x > -1e5 else []
+	if h.is_empty():
+		return []
+	var c: Dictionary = curves[int(h[0])]
+	var j := int(h[1])
+	var n := (c["ctrl"] as PackedVector3Array).size()
+	var can := str(c["kind"]) in ["line", "spline", "path", "arc"] and (bool(c.get("closed", false)) or (j > 0 and j < n - 1))
+	var sharp := point_sharp(c, j)
+	return [
+		["m_cv_pt_smooth", "Smooth point", "", "The curve runs through this point in a smooth bend (curved either side of it).", set_point_sharp.bind(int(h[0]), j, false), can and sharp],
